source: I think I'd do well with a scroll under each arm lecturing to young people. Don't you think?
...You know, now that you say it, I can picture it.
Let's be honest. I was never going to be King, nor did I have the desire for it.
Claudius seems to be invested in Denmark's future. I wish him all the best.
Well, with the proposal, certainly things have changed!
I've been thinking. Ought we to winter at our old estate?
It's old, and decrepit, and fallow. But His Majesty has bequeathed me a generous sum to have it refitted.
And you and Brit could manage the home, if you liked! ...It would certainly do your father proud.
At least, until Laertes is able to acquire an estate of his own. I've no doubt he'll make short work of that.
I'll think about it, Father.
At the very least, let's pay it a visit. We can start the big hearth and settle in for the snows.
Anything, and everything.
Before today, I didn't even dare to dream that she might accept me-- that we could be together.
But it's real, Ophelia. She accepted me. I want to build a world with her.
I want to take her somewhere far away from her father. Somewhere the Brockenhuus legacy will never be able to hurt her again.
She'll be a part of our family from now on.
And I know that someday soon, you two will come to love each other as dearly as I love her.
Ah. It's been a troublesome year, Ophelia.
But as the season trends towards autumn, I think often on my people...
I have failed them in the last few months. I thought the process of becoming a King a natural one.
Now I understand a kingdom must be earned—through work. Nothing in it is 'natural.' One must take great care with it.
I want to understand the needs of my people and help Denmark flourish.
And... I want... to understand what Hamlet needs, too.
I have reacted with dislike towards him in the past. But now all that must change. Let us build a new love, he and I.
Ah, me? Ay... I think I'd like to visit my sister.
It's been a long while. The both of us grow old. But watching Claudius mourn his brother, I've realized...
There is so little time in this world to show the ones we love how deeply we prize them.
It is long to Austria. A boat, then a carriage over land. But I believe it would be good to see her face once more before we die.
And then—I turn my thoughts to helping Claudius rule!
I never saw myself as a stateswoman, but Claudius believes I'm capable. It'll be a new role for me.
But a happy one, I think.
Oh, anywhere but here!
I find myself drawn back to Firenze. Back to my old masters, to the old workshops. To perhaps hold a brush once more.
Or perhaps I'll visit one of the great Italian universities and see if they'll have a poor old footsoldier like me.
My feet grow itchy to wander once more. It's time, I think. But I'll stay to see this evening's gala through.
It's nearly autumn. A whole new menu change shall soon arrive!
Thick stews, hearty rye bread, sausages as big around as my arm...
I aim to marvel every foreign dignitary who comes to dine at our table.
Let them see what Danish cuisine truly looks like!
Unfortunately, becoming related to you.
Not sure why I asked.
Hang on a moment. I was only joking.
I'm happy, Ophelia. For the first time in a long time.
I said and did things to you when I was in the depths of my unhappiness.
And I can never take those things back. I know I can't. If you hate me for them, I won't blame you an instant.
But your brother is an amazing man. And-- for what it's worth-- I think you and he are cut from the same cloth.
I'm sorry, I must have misheard you. Was that you paying me a compliment?
Hmm. Bask in the moment. It'll be gone soon, and you only get one compliment per decade, I've decided.
Regardless. Sisters?
So, what now?
Ah. you can still see me.
Of course. Ought I not to?
My son cannot see me any longer. He seems to have no memory of ever meeting me.
...It's for the best that way. They're happier, each of them.
But with Quince gone, why would you linger on?
Perhaps some outstanding task of mine still remains. I know not.
Either way, let us enjoy the world we have built, you and I. The others will never understand.
Excellent work, Ophelia.
To you as well, Your Majesty.
Hamlet. I need to ask you something.
Do you still-- did Claudius-- kill your father?
Ophelia, I know you like your games, but even that one's a bit cruel.
I miss Father as much as anyone.
You know, they might not have loved one another deeply, but... in the end, Claudius came to kiss him goodbye.
They say plague can be contagious. He risked his life for that small gesture.
Meanwhile, I had to be content with speaking to him through the door. They wouldn't let me inside.
(Plague? What is he talking about?)
(He seems to think-- his father died of plague?)
I'm sorry, Hamlet. I didn't mean to be hurtful. Please excuse me.
Father, can I ask something of you?
Has... Hamlet been acting strangely lately?
Why, if anything, he's twice the boy he was last summer.
He came from Wittenberg to see his father before the elder Hamlet passed of plague.
That's the sort of gesture I wouldn't have expected the wanton boy of a year ago to undertake.
But of course, I'm certain the grief will eventually wear on him in its own time.
Still -- he seems happy.
I see. Thank you, Father.
(So Father has no memory of Hamlet behaving oddly...)
(Does that mean Hamlet never met his father's ghost in this world?)
Laertes. Wait a moment.
Can you tell me what's happening to Denmark at the moment?
Is it true Norway asked for safe passage through Danish lands?
You're so strange sometimes, sister.
Come on. There's supper in the Hall.
And besides, I think Norway's rather too busy with their own civil war at the moment.
I don't believe we've had any affairs with that country since King Hamlet fought King Fortinbras years ago.
Whatever made you think of Norway, of all places?
Ah, never mind it. It was nothing.
Brit. Wait a moment.
Can't. Too hungry.
Is all this real?
What is happening right now? Am I in a dream?
If you are, then I'm in your dream too, which begs the question: Why are you <i>so<i> obsessed with me?
Fortunately for you, this is real as can be -- and we're missing the party.
The guards' quarters and our bedchambers are that way.
But I can't retire to my room until I find Laertes, like Father asked.
My room isn't down that way.
I'd better rest a while.
So little happened today, and yet my eyelids are already heavy.
Maybe it's all the 'advice' I received.
Father said Laertes was meeting with King Claudius.
That way leads to the grounds outside Elsinore. They wouldn't be out there.
Even in t his timeline, this bucket is still gross.
This bar's fireplace has a pleasent feel to it.
My father needs to meet with Laertes. Can you give him permission to leave this meeting?
Oh, are we on speaking terms now? You were the one who asked me to leave you alone.
Hamlet. That's all behind us. I need your help. Please.
I'm as much a prisoner to this awful meeting as your brother.
You'll have to talk to someone who has any power over my uncle. My Queen Mother, for instance.
My lady, my father wishes to speak with Laertes as soon as possible.
Oh, no! Have we run overlong? I'm sure Polonius is in an absolute fit...
Give me a moment. I'll whisper in my husband's ear.
Polonius wants me to retrieve Laertes for him.
Not now, girl! Be silent!
You are too bold.
Laertes is going to be late for his party.
(Oph—Lady Ophelia, I'm on duty at the moment. And must you be so loud?)
Something amiss, Bernardo?
N-nothing, my lord!
Laertes is trapped in a meeting, but my father wants to speak with him.
Ah! The good and fair Lady Ophelia. Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
Enough with the poetry, Horatio. You flatterer.
I was a poet in another life, you know. That was before I was a footsoldier. Then a student. Now I'm... what? A professional friend?
That's not a bad life. You've been many things at many times.
My apologies for the wallowing. You asked about your brother. Court's being held in the Great Hall, I believe.
...Oh. I suppose you're right.
Head there, and I'm certain you'll be able to tear him away.
...You know, back in Florence, there is no sense of 'lateness'.
Men arrive precisely when they mean to, and meals are six hours long!
I'd be much slower and larger if that were the case here.
Yes, bless Denmark. You Danes are always hurrying somewhere.
Laertes is meeting with the King, but my father needs him.
He's in the Great Hall, then. Have you been in there yet?
Ay, Maike... What's got your father all in a rush so?
Laertes heads to Paris tomorrow. I think Father's merely overly worried about his departure.
Is that so! Seems the boy has become a man, all in a flash. It's been so long since I chased him and Hamlet out of my kitchen with a broom.
Then again, probably for the better. My old back can hardly stand that kind of violence.
They were little terrors once upon a time. I'll miss him.
The Queen asked I have the food ready for the evening meal an hour ago—and yet, no one here. Least of all your brother.
My food does not wait for Danes. Danes wait for my food!
I'm going to look for Laertes, Father.
He'll be with the King, no doubt.
As I mentioned before...
Everything must go smoothly today!
I'm looking for my overly-tardy brother. Have you seen him around?
Marcellus! Are you all right?
Sorry, Lady Ophelia, yeh gave me a bit of a spook. Been on edge since last night.
Just, er... a difficult night's watch.
You look like you've seen a ghost, Marcellus. I'm sorry to have troubled you.
Been up a little too late playing cards again, have we?
No! Not at all. ... Irma cleaned me out after the last game. An' I haven't gone back to her for a game since.
Besides, some of the other boys thought that maybe, yeh know, the most senior guard ought not to gamble as much...
Well, I won't tell if you won't. Try to get some sleep tonight.
I'll try, I will...
As for yer brother...
I reckon he's meeting with m'lord the King to get formal permission for his trip to Paris.
Seems a strange thing to do on the eve of his departure.
